newsitem.title: SWEDEN: NCC to sell up to 75 pct Cityfastigheter.
newsitem.headline: NCC to sell up to 75 pct Cityfastigheter.

text.p: Sweden's second largest building company, NCC, said on Thursday it would sell up to 75 percent of property unit NK Cityfastigheter AB when it lists the company.
"This is part of NCC's strategy to reduce and concentrate its real estate portfolio and realising hidden values," NCC's chief executive, Jan Sjoqvist, said in a statement.
"It also reflects our ambition of participating in the restructuring of Sweden's real estate market."

NCC said earlier on Thursday that it would list NK Cityfastigheter, a real estate portfolio that consists of the NK department store buildings in Stockholm and Gothenburg and centrally located galleria buildings in four other cities.
NCC said the book value of the properties would be nearly 2.2 billion crowns and leasing value was 265 million crowns in 1996.
NCC said a preliminary price range for the shares would be announced on or around February 25 with a prospectus to be released on March 3.
The final price will set established through a public tender process and announced on March 14.
NCC said it expected NK Cityfastigheter shares to be listed on the Stockholm bourse's O list on March 24.
